channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Making Pre-Marital Medical Examinations Mandatory
item.description: Lawmakers in Kyrgyzstan are proposing to make free medical examinations mandatory before marriage registration. The initiative aims to facilitate early detection of infectious and hereditary diseases, and inform couples about their health status and potential risks to future children. The bill does not prohibit marriage based on medical results.

item.title: Foreign tech giants like Apple, OpenAI paid over 232 billion soms in taxes in Uzbekistan
item.description: Foreign companies providing electronic services in Uzbekistan paid 232.8 billion soms in taxes from January to September 2026, a 85% increase year-on-year. The number of foreign companies paying taxes grew to 109. Apple, Google, and Meta were the top three taxpayers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan proposes new rules for foreign land acquisition with real estate
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering new legislation to regulate land ownership for foreigners buying property. Under the proposed changes, foreigners could buy buildings and apartments, but the land beneath would be transferred to state or municipal ownership, granting only temporary usage rights.

item.title: Kazakhstan to develop new code of ethics for civil servants
item.description: Kazakhstan is set to introduce a new code of ethics for civil servants, based on constitutional requirements and principles of service to the state and society. The document is being developed jointly by the Presidential Administration, the Agency for Strategic Planning and Reforms, and the Kazakhstan Institute for Strategic Studies. Specific requirements and implementation dates are yet to be announced.

item.title: Kazakhstan to produce nearly 500 types of new medicines
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to launch the production of nearly 500 types of medicines through eight major investment projects, attracting $862 million in investment and creating over 1,200 new jobs. The Ministry of Health reported that the first phase, from 2027-2030, will see the production of 300 drug types. These initiatives aim to strengthen national drug security and expand the domestic pharmaceutical industry.

item.title: Kazakhstan Achieves Third Maturity Level in WHO Drug Regulation
item.description: The World Health Organization has confirmed Kazakhstan's drug regulation system meets international standards, achieving the third maturity level. This signifies a stable national regulatory system, making Kazakhstan the first CIS country to reach this stage. The achievement is expected to boost pharmaceutical exports and attract investment.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Increasing Hero Mother Pension Supplement to 5,000 Som
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a bill to increase the monthly pension supplement for mothers awarded the "Baatyr Ene" order from 1,000 to 5,000 som. The supplement, unchanged since 2011, aims to better support mothers raising seven or more children amidst rising living costs. Approximately 34,000 mothers would benefit.

item.title: Kazakhstan Resumes Oil Pumping via Atyrau-Samara Pipeline After Drone Attack
item.description: Kazakhstan has resumed oil transportation through the Atyrau-Samara main pipeline following a temporary halt due to a drone attack on Russian facilities. The pipeline was inspected and is now operating normally. The attack, which occurred on November 2, caused no casualties, according to Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement Digital Vaccine Cold Chain Monitoring by 2029
item.description: Kazakhstan will gradually implement a unified digital monitoring system for the vaccine cold chain starting this year, aiming for full completion by 2029. The system will control temperature conditions during vaccine storage and transportation, according to the Ministry of Health.

item.title: Kazakhstan PM Orders Clear Explanations for Patients on Drug Substitutions
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has instructed the Ministry of Health to provide clear explanations to patients when alternative medications are prescribed. He emphasized the importance of accessible information, especially for parents of children requiring long-term treatment, ensuring that information gaps do not become a burden.

item.title: Kazakhstan Begins 2027 Drug Procurement Three Months Early
item.description: Kazakhstan has initiated its 2027 drug procurement campaign three months ahead of schedule, with 84% of necessary medications already purchased by September. The Ministry of Health stated that warehouse needs will be fully met by year-end, and the non-reducible stock has been increased by 35% to prevent shortages.

item.title: Oil Transportation Resumes on Atyrau-Samara Pipeline After Drone Attack
item.description: Oil transportation has resumed on the Atyrau-Samara main oil pipeline in a normal mode, according to the Ministry of Energy. Pumping was restored after technical inspection work was completed. The pipeline, part of the Uzen-Atyrau-Samara system, was temporarily halted on November 2 due to a drone attack in Russia.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China eye joint fund of $200 million for Trans-Caspian transport route
item.description: Kazakhstan's Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin discussed the creation of a joint investment fund for the development of the Trans-Caspian International Transport Route (TITR) with China's Finance Minister Lan Foan. The proposed fund aims for an initial target volume of up to $200 million.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Strategic Uranium Reserve for Future Nuclear Power Plants by End of 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to form a strategic uranium reserve by the end of 2027 to supply its future nuclear power plants. These plants will be built by Russia's Rosatom and China's CNNC. The country also aims to sign an intergovernmental agreement for the Moynqum nuclear power plant and prepare qualified personnel.

item.title: Asian Cup Football Tournament Rescheduled to January 2028
item.description: The Asian Cup football tournament, originally scheduled for January 7-February 5, 2027, has been postponed. Due to the unstable situation in the Middle East, the tournament will now take place from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028.

item.title: Atyrau-Samara oil pipeline resumes operation after disruption
item.description: The Atyrau-Samara oil pipeline has resumed its operations. The pipeline is a crucial link for transporting oil. Further details on the cause of the disruption or the duration of the outage were not immediately available.

item.title: Uzbekistan expands Work and Travel program to technicum students
item.description: Uzbekistan will allow technicum students to participate in the Work and Travel international program, enabling them to work and travel abroad. This initiative, detailed in a government decree, opens opportunities in countries like the EU, South Korea, Japan, UK, US, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand.

item.title: Kazakhstan tungsten project valued at $2 billion, Trump sons have minor stake
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kaz Resources tungsten project is planning an IPO on a US stock exchange by 2027, with an estimated valuation of $2 billion. Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump will hold a less than 1% indirect stake in the project through investment agreements.

item.title: Kazakhstan Promises Equal Access to Agrologistics Centers by 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to ensure long-term financing for agricultural development programs, including livestock, processing, and tractor production. Deputy Prime Minister Serik Zhumangarin announced that by 2027, all agricultural producers will have equal access to agrologistics center infrastructure. A national water resource information system is also set to be completed by March 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Has Secured Over 80% of Necessary Medications for 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan has procured 84% of the required volume of medications for 2027 by September. The Ministry of Health has increased the non-depletable stock of medicines to mitigate the risk of shortages. This information was shared by Health Minister Akmaral Alnazarova during a government meeting.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Fines for Forcing Teachers into Unrelated Work
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering introducing fines for compelling teachers to perform non-teaching duties like cleaning or repairs. The proposed legislation also aims to protect educators from retaliation if they refuse such tasks. Additionally, it seeks to ease school uniform requirements and prohibit barring students from classes due to attire.

item.title: Drug Market Violations in Kazakhstan Increased Tenfold This Year
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Health reported a tenfold increase in drug market violations this year, with 788 entities found non-compliant. Violations include reintroducing drugs into circulation, selling free medications, and exceeding price limits. The ministry noted a twentyfold decrease in the sale of free medicines in pharmacies due to implemented measures.

item.title: Iran Plans New Four-Nation Meeting on Afghanistan Amid Regional Diplomatic Efforts
item.description: Iran is preparing to host a new four-country meeting on Afghanistan in the coming months. The meeting aims to discuss Afghanistan's security, political situation, and future cooperation. Previous meetings under this format have involved Iran, Russia, China, and Pakistan.

item.title: Over Two Thousand Firearms Confiscated from Illegal Circulation Since Year's Start
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that over two thousand firearms have been confiscated from illegal circulation this year. Police also seized over 23 tons of fish, including sturgeon, and 345 hunting weapons during anti-poaching operations.

item.title: 11 Kazakh Children Hospitalized in Tashkent During Football Tournament
item.description: Eleven Kazakh children and six adults were hospitalized in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, after falling ill during an international football tournament. The young athletes reported symptoms including fever and diarrhea on October 31st. Parents suspect food poisoning from their hotel and have complained about initial hospital conditions. They are requesting the children's return to Kazakhstan.

item.title: Domestic Violence Discussion Intensifies After Woman's Murder in Batken
item.description: Following the murder of a 24-year-old woman by her husband in Kyrgyzstan's Batken region, a discussion has erupted regarding domestic violence and parental pressure to stay in abusive relationships. The victim had reportedly complained of abuse to her mother before her death. Social media users are also sharing a video of a religious figure advising tolerance towards marital violence.

item.title: Uzbekistan Anti-Corruption Investigator Arrested for Alleged $100,000 Bribe
item.description: An investigator with the Anti-Corruption Department in Fergana, Uzbekistan, has been apprehended on suspicion of accepting a $100,000 bribe. The bribe was allegedly offered to reduce the amount of damages in a criminal case and to cancel an arrest warrant for the accused. The investigation is ongoing.

item.title: Kazakhstan Resumes Oil Pumping on Atyrau-Samara Route After Technical Checks
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy announced the resumption of oil pumping through the Atyrau-Samara pipeline following a technical inspection. Pumping was temporarily halted due to a drone attack on a Russian facility. Operations are now proceeding normally, and the ministry continues to monitor the situation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Simplifies Drug Registration and Pricing Procedures from 2026
item.description: Kazakhstan will simplify drug registration and pricing procedures starting in 2026, integrating them into a single "one-stop-shop" service. The Ministry of Health announced that registration for drugs from developed countries will take 15 working days. The country can also independently initiate drug registration for rare diseases.

item.title: Kazakhstan Oil Terminal Operations Halted Due to Drone Incident
item.description: Loading operations at Kazakhstan's oil terminal were temporarily halted due to a drone incident. The Ministry of Energy confirmed that all checks were completed and operations have resumed. No restrictions were placed on oil reception from Kazakh shippers.

item.title: First International Coal Industry Forum to be Held in Dushanbe on December 9
item.description: Tajikistan's first international coal industry forum will take place in Dushanbe on December 9, 2026, at the Hyatt Regency Dushanbe hotel. The event will be attended by government officials, financial institutions, and business representatives. The Ministry of Industry and New Technologies invites interested parties to register.

item.title: Tajikistan's Defense Ministry Reports 97% Fulfillment of Fall Conscription Plan
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Defense announced that over 97 percent of the fall conscription plan was met in the first month. Regions like Gorno-Badakhshan, Khatlon, and Dushanbe achieved 100% fulfillment. The conscription targets men aged 18-27.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Investigator Arrested for Allegedly Accepting $100,000 Bribe
item.description: An investigator from the Department for Combating Economic Crimes in Fergana, Uzbekistan, has been arrested on suspicion of accepting a $100,000 bribe. State Security Service reported the arrest. The investigator allegedly promised to influence a criminal case, reduce damages, and cancel a search warrant. A criminal case has been initiated against him for accepting a large bribe.

item.title: French Companies Offer Innovations for Uzbekistan's Urban Development
item.description: French companies are ready to expand their operations in Uzbekistan, offering innovations in urban development and transport. Gerard Wolf, Special Representative of the French Minister of Europe and Foreign Affairs, met with Uzbek officials to discuss cooperation. He highlighted French expertise in sustainable cities and smart solutions, emphasizing the potential for collaboration in modernizing Uzbek cities and infrastructure.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev to Visit Bukhara Region
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev will visit the Bukhara region on Tuesday, according to the presidential press service. The head of state will review efforts to preserve historical heritage and develop tourism infrastructure, as well as prospective projects in industry and agriculture. The two-day visit includes a video conference on launching new capacities and developing the region.

item.title: Kazakhstan Detains 10 Suspected of Extremism in Atyrau
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) reported the detention of 10 individuals in Atyrau on suspicion of forming an extremist group, promoting terrorism, and inciting religious hatred. The KNB claims the detainees intended to violently alter the constitutional order in the country's western region. During searches, firearms, drugs, and religious materials were seized.

item.title: Tajikistan to Receive $200 Million Loan from Eurasian Fund for Budget Support
item.description: The Eurasian Fund for Stabilization and Development (EFSD) will provide Tajikistan with a $200 million loan to support the state budget. The agreement for these funds was signed on August 13th. This loan is intended to help replenish the country's budget over 20 years with a 1% interest rate.

item.title: Iran Reports Ongoing Contacts with US to End War After Talks Stall
item.description: Iran stated that contacts with the United States to end their eight-month war are continuing, following talks with Qatari mediators that ended without a breakthrough. Tehran presented its conditions and proposals, awaiting Washington's political rationality. Both China and Russia opposed renewed military action.

item.title: Faiq: Women and Youth Must Have a Role in Afghanistan's Future Decisions
item.description: Faiq emphasized the crucial need for women and youth to actively participate in future decision-making processes within Afghanistan. This call highlights the importance of their inclusion in shaping the country's direction and policies moving forward.

item.title: Geological Exploration Underway for Gold Processing Plant in Pendjikent, Tajikistan
item.description: LLC "Panchzar" is conducting geological exploration in the Mosarif area of Pendjikent, Tajikistan, to establish a gold processing plant. The initiative aligns with the government's focus on utilizing mineral resources. Local officials visited the site, where 20 specialists are currently involved in the research.
